Observed:
- Polyarthritis and joint swelling
- Progressive dyspnea with orthopnea
- Pulmonary hypertension with elevated PASP
- Autoantibody positivity with anti-centromere antibodies
- 58-year-old woman
- 2-month history of fatigue, weakness, polyarthritis, and joint swelling
- 9-month history of idiopathic pulmonary hypertension
- Progressive dyspnea over 3 years
- NYHA class IV
- Orthopnea without cough or sputum
- Low-grade fever and night sweats
- Echocardiography showed PASP of 80 mm Hg
- Left ventricular ejection fraction of 60%
- Mild mitral regurgitation and moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation
- Chest CT showed alveolar infiltrates and peripheral lung nodules
- Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 45 mm/h
- Antinuclear antibody titer of 1:320
- Anti-centromere antibody level of 94.8 AU/ml
- Raynaud’s phenomenon elicited by cold-water immersion
Differential diagnosis:
1. Limited Systemic Sclerosis
2. Systemic Sclerosis
3. CREST Syndrome
4. Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
5. Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension associated with Connective Tissue Disease
